coverage.assessment: The proposal now jumps from the Embassy invitation to 'marry me' without the contrastive link, so the Embassy reads as a non sequitur. Tommy's 'I owe you something' loses the stated manoeuvre that makes it a payback. Job, money and furnishing setups otherwise hold.

The Rolls-Royce and the taxi both go via Regent's Park. 'Head over ears' is said first by Julius, then by Tuppence. Carter's Government job and Julius's ranch post are correctly assigned. Dropping 'In the meantime' is covered by 'also returning'.

Attribution is clear throughout. 'Ours' is Tuppence's and Tommy has the last line. The revision cut the 'Rather fun, wasn't it?' / 'Rather.' small-talk exchange that dramatized the constraint, so 'essayed' now carries the effort alone.
No changed facts. 'In America' is dropped from the ranch post, but the London contrast survives. The patience promise and the 'set you free' condition are intact.
Tuppence's 'I expect he's proposing to her now' is cut. That line gave the reader the dramatic irony of having just witnessed the proposal.

The ironic aside and the coloured speech tags survive. Christie's oblique handling of the kiss (raised face, taxi circling the north side of the park) is gone, and Jane's coy 'I don't know London very well' is trimmed.
The two-couple mirror ends with the taxi's detour unechoed. Tommy's sentiment line no longer explicitly reverses the roles by making Tuppence speak sentimentally first.
All six local endpoints and their partner endpoints survive in the revised drafts. Dependency 0 survives textually but with weakened force (see F2).

strengths: Julius's hustling comedy is intact: the special license 'to-morrow morning' comes immediately before 'I don't want to hustle you any'.
All eight verbatim anchors survive exactly, including the trailing ellipsis on Jane's acceptance and the emphasized '_Ours_'.
The 'head over ears' echo runs in the right order, from Julius to Tuppence, and the Carter-job / Julius-ranch assignment is correct.
The uncle line is cut cleanly while 'hastily creating a diversion' keeps the job question framed as a diversion, as the plan requires.
summary: The revision keeps every verbatim anchor, the two-car Regent's Park parallel, the job and money facts, and the closing 'sport' exchange. No speaker or fact errors appear. Its further cuts below the first draft remove several small hinges that the comedy and romance depend on: the 'another plan' link that turns the Embassy mention into an alternative, Tommy's 'I was determined to make you say it', the oblique kiss as the taxi circles the park, and Tuppence's cross-cutting 'proposing to her now'. These are short, restorable losses rather than blockers.
